_comment: summaries: category -> home-card text; names: slug -> display name; titles: category/slug -> fallback title when the md has no "## " title; iconOverrides: slug -> icon URL (fetch skips web sources for these slugs). videoOverrides: category/slug -> local filename (from that category assets/), served from /content/<category>/ when the GitHub user-attachments URL is dead. siteUrl: custom domain base (e.g. https://example.com) — enables canonical URLs, og:url and sitemap.xml when set. meta: siteName = suffix for page titles / embed headings; description = home meta description (SEO only, not visible).

summaries.account_takeover: Bugs that let an attacker take over someone's account — sometimes with nothing more than a clicked link.
summaries.bac: Broken Access Control: apps that fail to check you're allowed to touch a resource, like sending messages to channels you can't write to from the dashboard.
summaries.broken_authentication: Missing or bypassable authentication checks — getting an identity without the credentials that should be required for it.
summaries.code_injection: Injecting code or commands (shell injection, unsafe deserialization, ...) to get execution as the user running the app.
summaries.cves: Apps running outdated software with known CVEs (CVE-YYYY-XXXXX) that still worked exactly as published.
summaries.mass_assignment: Setting object properties the server never meant to be editable by sending extra fields — from guild ownership to Discord API options.
summaries.open_redirect: Unvalidated `redirect` parameters that send you anywhere after a trusted flow (like an OAuth authorization) — mostly useful for phishing.
summaries.path_cancel: User input embedded into request URIs: dot segments cancel and rewrite the path before it reaches the Discord API, turning benign features into arbitrary API calls.
summaries.prototype_pollution: Polluting JavaScript object prototypes (`__proto__`) to make apps behave in ways their developers never wrote.
summaries.query_injection: Injecting SQL/NoSQL operators into database queries to extract data or flip boolean logic.
summaries.ssrf: Server-Side Request Forgery: making the server send requests to internal services it was never supposed to reach.
summaries.xss: Cross-Site Scripting: injecting JavaScript into apps to hijack sessions and do mischief as other users.
